correctness.rationale: The identity D_n=sum_k binom(n,k)^2*2^k yields digitwise D_n≡∏D_(n_j) (mod p) by Lucas/Fermat. For prime p>=5, 0,1,p-1 are allowed digit residues. Let a=p-|Z_p|, c=#adjacent allowed digits d,d+1 for d<=p-2. Among 0<=nB on a density-one set. Independent direct integral recurrence tested the exact p and p² counts for primes 5,7,11,13,17,19 up to n<500; confirmed Z7={3}, the 7² count 6. The proof alone establishes all p,L. An additional independent direct integer recurrence counted 84 adjacent multiples of seven below 7^3, exactly as the formula predicts.

evidence: Noe, JIS 9 (2006) Article 06.2.7 proves single-index divisibility for all generalized central trinomials, hence covers the digit criterion of central Delannoy. Z.-W. Sun arXiv:1009.2486 addresses Delannoy sums and congruences.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader coefficient family of Noe is stronger for single-index divisibility but does not explicitly assert a two-consecutive-index joint distribution. A general theorem counting neighboring zeros of automatic sequences could imply this specialization; preserve risk.

Full Eu paper or general joint automatic-sequence machinery could dominate.

originality.rationale: Noe (2006) Theorem 8.5 already gives the all-digit one-point p-divisibility criterion for generalized central trinomial numbers (including Delannoy), and this is fully credited. Inspected source neither formulates consecutive-index carry counts nor the density-one unbounded neighboring gcd. The present joint distribution and the use of a forbidden midpoint for p≡3 mod4 constitute the assessed additional claim, subject to possible known automatic-sequence or neighboring-gcd equivalents.

value.rationale: The gcd of consecutive terms of a familiar combinatorial sequence is a natural exact arithmetic invariant. The prime-power block formula gives all joint zero frequencies and, for each p≡3 mod4, implies almost-sure-in-density simultaneous divisibility; combining primes proves the striking density-one unboundedness of consecutive gcds. This is a motivated distributional strengthening of the known single-index Lucas condition, not a mere small-n recomputation.
